ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is a bar comparison chart, with the horizontal axis arranged by five groups: A, B, C, D, and E; the legend shows three types of indicators, namely area (10,000 hm²), yield per unit area (kg/hm²), and total output. Observing the C group, C's yield-per-unit-area bar is labeled about 2656 kg/hm², the total-output bar is relatively high, labeled about 7454, and the area bar is also not the smallest, overall presenting the wheat production characteristics of “high total output, medium yield per unit area, and relatively large planting area.” Then reason: the question stem limits the five countries to the United States, Canada, China, Denmark, and India. Combining common knowledge of wheat production, China usually has the highest total output and relatively high area and yield per unit area; Denmark has a very small area but high yield per unit area; Canada has a relatively large area but relatively low total output; India has a relatively large area and high total output but low yield per unit area. C shows relatively high total output, medium yield per unit area, and relatively large area, which better fits the wheat production characteristics of the United States. Therefore, C represents the United States.
